name: Brief Fidelity Eval

# Runs the promptfoo brief-vs-digest fidelity eval. Not part of the per-push merge
# gate: it makes live Claude calls (costs credits), so it runs weekly and on demand.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'  # Mondays 06:00 UTC

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7

      - name: Install Python library
        run: uv sync --dev

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Install eval dependencies
        # promptfoo lives in its own dependency island (eval/) so it stays out of
        # the CDK/Lambda build's npm tree. See eval/README.md.
        run: npm --prefix eval ci

      - name: Run promptfoo fidelity eval
        working-directory: eval
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        # The eval script sets PROMPTFOO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python so the provider
        # runs synthesize() via uv's venv at the repo root.
        # One retry: "Could not extract JSON from llm-rubric response" is a transient
        # promptfoo grader-parse failure unrelated to brief quality.
        run: |
          npm run eval -- --output eval-results.json || {
            echo "First attempt failed; retrying once…"
            npm run eval -- --output eval-results.json
          }

      - name: Upload eval results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: brief-eval-results
          path: eval/eval-results.json
          if-no-files-found: warn

# RSS Brief fidelity eval

A [promptfoo](https://promptfoo.dev) eval that continuously checks the **RSS Brief**
against the **digest** it was synthesised from. It drives the real Python pipeline
(`rss_email.brief_generator.synthesize`) via a custom provider, so it measures the
shipping code rather than a copy of the prompt.

## What it checks

| Assertion | Type | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is-json` | built-in | The synthesis output is valid JSON. |
| `schema.cjs` | deterministic | All category keys are canonical (no `AI_ML`), `AI/ML` is present, every `signal_strength` is valid. |
| `major_coverage.cjs` | deterministic | Every story in the fixture's `expected_major.json` is surfaced — major news is not dropped. |
| `source_ranking.cjs` | deterministic | High-tier sources (blogs / Hacker News / Reddit) are not under-represented vs the digest. Tiers come from `../src/rss_email/brief_config.json`. |
| faithfulness | llm-rubric | Every claim/number/entity in the brief is supported by the digest — nothing fabricated. |
| relevance | llm-rubric | `relevance_to_reader` is null or genuinely tied to the profile, never forced. |

## Dependencies

promptfoo lives in **this directory's own** `package.json` / `package-lock.json`, separate
from the repo-root `package.json`. This keeps promptfoo's large transitive tree (mongodb,
googleapis, …) out of the CDK/Lambda deployment build, whose `npm ci` must stay clean.
Always run the eval from `eval/` — the npm scripts assume that working directory, and the
config's paths (`provider.py`, `assertions/`, `fixtures/`, `../src/...`) are relative to it.

## Run

```bash
uv sync --dev                    # repo-root .venv with anthropic/pydantic (the provider uses it)
npm --prefix eval ci             # installs promptfoo into eval/node_modules
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
npm --prefix eval run eval       # runs from eval/ (the script sets PROMPTFOO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python)
npm --prefix eval run eval:view  # opens the promptfoo web UI for the last run
```

Or, equivalently, from inside `eval/`: `npm ci && ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... npm run eval`.

Each run makes a handful of Claude calls (one synthesis per fixture + the llm-rubric
grader), so it is not wired into the per-push CI gate. It runs weekly and on demand via
[`.github/workflows/eval.yml`](../.github/workflows/eval.yml).

## Add a fixture

A fixture is one day's digest in the same shape `build_synthesis_input` produces:

```
eval/fixtures/<YYYY-MM-DD>/
  digest_articles.json   # { "AI/ML": [ {title, url, summary, source}, ... ], ... }
  expected_major.json    # { "must_cover": [ "<exact major-story title>", ... ] }
  digest_text.txt        # readable digest used as the faithfulness grader's source
```

The quickest way to capture one is from a live run:

```bash
# Dump the categorised synthesis input the brief actually received.
uv run python src/cli_brief_generator.py --dry-run --days 1 --debug
```

Then add a matching `tests:` entry in `promptfooconfig.yaml`.

# Fix the failing Brief Fidelity Eval workflow

## Context

The `Brief Fidelity Eval` workflow (`.github/workflows/eval.yml`, weekly on Mondays) has
failed on every scheduled run since 2026-07-27 — three consecutive weeks. It never reaches
the eval itself; it dies during dependency install:

```
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and
npm error package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync.
npm error Missing: gcp-metadata@7.0.1 from lock file
```

### Root cause (reproduced locally)

`mongoose → mongodb` declares `gcp-metadata ^7.0.1` as an **optional peer dependency**:

```
node_modules/mongoose/node_modules/mongodb  [peerDependencies]  gcp-metadata ^7.0.1
                                            peerDependenciesMeta: { optional: true }
```

- **npm 10** materialises optional peer deps, so it expects a
  `node_modules/mongoose/node_modules/gcp-metadata` entry in the lockfile.
- **npm 11** does not, so a lockfile it writes omits that entry.

`eval.yml` pins `node-version: '22'`, whose bundled npm is **10.9.8**. Dependabot now
regenerates lockfiles with **npm 11**. Every Dependabot PR against `/eval` (`#45`–`#49`)
therefore writes a lockfile that CI's npm 10 rejects — and those PRs merge green because no
PR workflow runs `npm --prefix eval ci`.

Commit `448246b` briefly restored the entry (hand-run install with an older npm), which is
why one run in between looked healthier; the next Dependabot bump removed it again.

Verified by direct reproduction on `origin/main`'s `eval/package-lock.json`:

| npm | result |
| --- | --- |
| 10.9.8 (Node 22, what CI uses) | `EUSAGE — Missing: gcp-metadata@7.0.1` |
| 11.11.0 (Node 24, local dev) | `added 693 packages` ✅ |

Also confirmed npm 11 installs the *older* npm-10-style lockfile fine — npm 11 is strictly
the more tolerant validator, so moving CI forward is safe in both directions.

Scoped checks that are **not** affected: the repo-root `package-lock.json` (68 packages, no
optional peer deps) installs cleanly under npm 10, so `Lint and Test` and `Test CDK Synth`
(both Node 20) stay as they are.

### Intended outcome

The weekly eval installs its dependencies and actually runs the fidelity assertions again.

## Change

Single edit — `.github/workflows/eval.yml`, the `Setup Node.js` step:

```yaml
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          # Node 24 bundles npm 11, matching the lockfile format Dependabot and local
          # dev write. Node 22's npm 10 rejects it (it wants mongodb's optional peer
          # dep gcp-metadata@7.0.1 materialised in the lock).
          node-version: '24'
```

Leave everything else in the workflow alone — `npm ci` stays (determinism is the point),
and the existing one-retry wrapper around `npm run eval` still covers transient
`llm-rubric` grader-parse failures.

Optionally add a one-line note to `eval/README.md`'s **Dependencies** section that the
lockfile is npm 11 format, so a future contributor on npm 10 knows why `npm ci` complains.

Per your decision, no PR-triggered lockfile check is being added; the trade-off is that the
next lockfile-format drift is again only surfaced by the weekly scheduled run.

## Implementation notes

- The local checkout is **3 commits behind** `origin/main` (local `b671742`, remote
  `9d10095`). Pull before branching — the broken lockfiles only exist upstream.
- Branch off `main`, single-file commit, PR as usual.

## Verification

1. **Reproduce the failure first** (proves the fix is the fix):

   ```bash
   cd /tmp && rm -rf npmcheck && mkdir npmcheck && cd npmcheck
   git -C ~/code/rss-email show origin/main:eval/package.json      > package.json
   git -C ~/code/rss-email show origin/main:eval/package-lock.json > package-lock.json
   npx --yes --package npm@10.9.8 -c 'npm ci --ignore-scripts'   # expect EUSAGE
   npm ci --ignore-scripts                                        # npm 11 → succeeds
   ```

2. **Confirm the workflow parses and installs** — after merging, trigger it manually:

   ```bash
   gh workflow run eval.yml
   gh run watch $(gh run list --workflow=eval.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')
   ```

   The `Install eval dependencies` step must complete instead of erroring at `npm ci`.

3. **Confirm the eval itself still passes.** This is a genuinely open question: the
   assertions have not run to completion since 2026-07-20, and the run before that
   (2026-07-13, `29237222532`) failed with `✗ 1 failed (100%)` on both the first attempt
   and the retry — an assertion failure, not an install failure. If step 2 now surfaces a
   red assertion, that is a **separate, pre-existing issue** with brief quality or the
   fixture, to be triaged from the uploaded `brief-eval-results.json` artifact:

   ```bash
   gh run download <run-id> -n brief-eval-results
   ```

4. **Local end-to-end** (optional, spends Claude credits):

   ```bash
   uv sync --dev
   npm --prefix eval ci
   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... npm --prefix eval run eval
   ```

# RSS Brief fidelity eval

A [promptfoo](https://promptfoo.dev) eval that continuously checks the **RSS Brief**
against the **digest** it was synthesised from. It drives the real Python pipeline
(`rss_email.brief_generator.synthesize`) via a custom provider, so it measures the
shipping code rather than a copy of the prompt.

## What it checks

| Assertion | Type | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is-json` | built-in | The synthesis output is valid JSON. |
| `schema.cjs` | deterministic | All category keys are canonical (no `AI_ML`), `AI/ML` is present, every `signal_strength` is valid. |
| `major_coverage.cjs` | deterministic | Every story in the fixture's `expected_major.json` is surfaced — major news is not dropped. |
| `source_ranking.cjs` | deterministic | High-tier sources (blogs / Hacker News / Reddit) are not under-represented vs the digest. Tiers come from `../src/rss_email/brief_config.json`. |
| faithfulness | llm-rubric | Every claim/number/entity in the brief is supported by the digest — nothing fabricated. |
| relevance | llm-rubric | `relevance_to_reader` is null or genuinely tied to the profile, never forced. |

## Dependencies

promptfoo lives in **this directory's own** `package.json` / `package-lock.json`, separate
from the repo-root `package.json`. This keeps promptfoo's large transitive tree (mongodb,
googleapis, …) out of the CDK/Lambda deployment build, whose `npm ci` must stay clean.
Always run the eval from `eval/` — the npm scripts assume that working directory, and the
config's paths (`provider.py`, `assertions/`, `fixtures/`, `../src/...`) are relative to it.

## Run

```bash
uv sync --dev                    # repo-root .venv with anthropic/pydantic (the provider uses it)
npm --prefix eval ci             # installs promptfoo into eval/node_modules
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
npm --prefix eval run eval       # runs from eval/ (the script sets PROMPTFOO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python)
npm --prefix eval run eval:view  # opens the promptfoo web UI for the last run
```

Or, equivalently, from inside `eval/`: `npm ci && ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... npm run eval`.

Each run makes a handful of Claude calls (one synthesis per fixture + the llm-rubric
grader), so it is not wired into the per-push CI gate. It runs weekly and on demand via
[`.github/workflows/eval.yml`](../.github/workflows/eval.yml).

## Add a fixture

A fixture is one day's digest in the same shape `build_synthesis_input` produces:

```
eval/fixtures/<YYYY-MM-DD>/
  digest_articles.json   # { "AI/ML": [ {title, url, summary, source}, ... ], ... }
  expected_major.json    # { "must_cover": [ "<exact major-story title>", ... ] }
  digest_text.txt        # readable digest used as the faithfulness grader's source
```

The quickest way to capture one is from a live run:

```bash
# Dump the categorised synthesis input the brief actually received.
uv run python src/cli_brief_generator.py --dry-run --days 1 --debug
```

Then add a matching `tests:` entry in `promptfooconfig.yaml`.

jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - name: Install uv

      - name: Install Python library

# RSS Brief fidelity eval

A [promptfoo](https://promptfoo.dev) eval that continuously checks the **RSS Brief**
against the **digest** it was synthesised from. It drives the real Python pipeline
(`rss_email.brief_generator.synthesize`) via a custom provider, so it measures the
shipping code rather than a copy of the prompt.

## What it checks

| Assertion | Type | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is-json` | built-in | The synthesis output is valid JSON. |
| `schema.cjs` | deterministic | All category keys are canonical (no `AI_ML`), `AI/ML` is present, every `signal_strength` is valid. |
| `major_coverage.cjs` | deterministic | Every story in the fixture's `expected_major.json` is surfaced — major news is not dropped. |
| `source_ranking.cjs` | deterministic | High-tier sources (blogs / Hacker News / Reddit) are not under-represented vs the digest. Tiers come from `../src/rss_email/brief_config.json`. |
| faithfulness | llm-rubric | Every claim/number/entity in the brief is supported by the digest — nothing fabricated. |
| relevance | llm-rubric | `relevance_to_reader` is null or genuinely tied to the profile, never forced. |

## Dependencies

promptfoo lives in **this directory's own** `package.json` / `package-lock.json`, separate
from the repo-root `package.json`. This keeps promptfoo's large transitive tree (mongodb,
googleapis, …) out of the CDK/Lambda deployment build, whose `npm ci` must stay clean.
Always run the eval from `eval/` — the npm scripts assume that working directory, and the
config's paths (`provider.py`, `assertions/`, `fixtures/`, `../src/...`) are relative to it.

`package-lock.json` here needs **npm 11** (Node 24). Dependabot writes it with npm 11, and
npm 11 stopped recording optional peer dependencies — so npm 10 fails `npm ci` with
`Missing: gcp-metadata@7.0.1 from lock file` (mongodb declares it as an optional peer).

## Run

```bash
uv sync --dev                    # repo-root .venv with anthropic/pydantic (the provider uses it)
npm --prefix eval ci             # installs promptfoo into eval/node_modules
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
npm --prefix eval run eval       # runs from eval/ (the script sets PROMPTFOO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python)
npm --prefix eval run eval:view  # opens the promptfoo web UI for the last run
```

Or, equivalently, from inside `eval/`: `npm ci && ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... npm run eval`.

Each run makes a handful of Claude calls (one synthesis per fixture + the llm-rubric
grader), so it is not wired into the per-push CI gate. It runs weekly and on demand via
[`.github/workflows/eval.yml`](../.github/workflows/eval.yml).

## Add a fixture

A fixture is one day's digest in the same shape `build_synthesis_input` produces:

```
eval/fixtures/<YYYY-MM-DD>/
  digest_articles.json   # { "AI/ML": [ {title, url, summary, source}, ... ], ... }
  expected_major.json    # { "must_cover": [ "<exact major-story title>", ... ] }
  digest_text.txt        # readable digest used as the faithfulness grader's source
```

The quickest way to capture one is from a live run:

```bash
# Dump the categorised synthesis input the brief actually received.
uv run python src/cli_brief_generator.py --dry-run --days 1 --debug
```

Then add a matching `tests:` entry in `promptfooconfig.yaml`.

`Brief Fidelity Eval` has failed on **every scheduled run since 2026-07-27** (3 weeks). It never reaches the eval — it dies during dependency install:

```
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and
npm error package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync.
npm error Missing: gcp-metadata@7.0.1 from lock file

## Root cause

`mongoose → mongodb` declares `gcp-metadata ^7.0.1` as an **optional peer dependency**:

```
node_modules/mongoose/node_modules/mongodb  [peerDependencies]  gcp-metadata ^7.0.1
                                            peerDependenciesMeta: { optional: true }
```

- npm **< 11.5** materialises optional peer deps, so it expects a `mongoose/node_modules/gcp-metadata` entry in the lockfile.
- npm **>= 11.5** no longer records them.

`eval.yml` pinned `node-version: '22'` → npm **10.9.8**. Dependabot regenerates lockfiles with a current npm. So every Dependabot bump against `/eval` (#45–#49) wrote a lockfile that the eval job then rejected — and those PRs merged green, because no PR workflow runs `npm --prefix eval ci`.

Commit 448246b briefly restored the entry by hand, which is why one run in between looked healthier; the next bump removed it again.

## Fix

Bump the eval workflow to Node 24 (npm 11.17), aligning CI with the npm that writes the lockfile.

## Verification

Reproduced against the current `eval/package-lock.json`, one npm version at a time:

| npm | result |
| --- | --- |
| 10.9.8 (Node 22 — what CI used) | ❌ `Missing: gcp-metadata@7.0.1` |
| 11.0.0 / 11.3.0 / 11.4.0 | ❌ same |
| 11.5.0 / 11.6.x / 11.9.0 / 11.11.0 | ✅ installs |
| **11.17.0 (Node 24.19 — what CI gets)** | ✅ `added 691 packages` |

So the floor is npm 11.5.0 → Node >= 24.5; `'24'` resolves to the latest 24.x, currently 24.19. Noted in the workflow comment so a future pin doesn't drop below it.

Also confirmed npm 11 installs the *older* npm-10-style lockfile fine, so moving forward is safe in both directions.

## Scope

- The repo-root `package-lock.json` (68 packages, no optional peer deps) installs cleanly under npm 10, so `Lint and Test` and `Test CDK Synth` stay on Node 20.
- No PR-triggered lockfile check added (per review decision) — the trade-off is that the next lockfile-format drift is again only caught by the weekly scheduled run.

## Note — a separate pre-existing issue may surface

The eval's assertions have not run to completion since 2026-07-20. The run before that (2026-07-13, `29237222532`) failed with `✗ 1 failed (100%)` on both the attempt and the retry — an *assertion* failure, not an install failure. If the first green install now surfaces a red assertion, that is a distinct brief-quality/fixture issue, triageable from the uploaded `brief-eval-results.json` artifact.
EOF

name: Brief Fidelity Eval

# Runs the promptfoo brief-vs-digest fidelity eval. Not part of the per-push merge
# gate: it makes live Claude calls (costs credits), so it runs weekly and on demand.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'  # Mondays 06:00 UTC

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7

      - name: Install Python library
        run: uv sync --dev

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          # eval/package-lock.json is written by npm 11 (Dependabot and local dev), which
          # no longer records optional peer deps. Older npm then fails `npm ci` with
          # "Missing: gcp-metadata@7.0.1" — mongodb declares it as an optional peer.
          # Needs npm >= 11.5.0 (11.4.0 still fails), i.e. Node >= 24.5; '24' resolves to
          # the latest 24.x, currently 24.19 / npm 11.17. Do not pin below that.
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Install eval dependencies
        # promptfoo lives in its own dependency island (eval/) so it stays out of
        # the CDK/Lambda build's npm tree. See eval/README.md.
        run: npm --prefix eval ci

      - name: Run promptfoo fidelity eval
        working-directory: eval
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
        # The eval script sets PROMPTFOO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python so the provider
        # runs synthesize() via uv's venv at the repo root.
        # One retry: "Could not extract JSON from llm-rubric response" is a transient
        # promptfoo grader-parse failure unrelated to brief quality.
        run: |
          npm run eval -- --output eval-results.json || {
            echo "First attempt failed; retrying once…"
            npm run eval -- --output eval-results.json
          }

      - name: Upload eval results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: brief-eval-results
          path: eval/eval-results.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
